Prof. Khalid Fakhro recognized for pioneering contributions to genomic research and his leadership in advancing precision medicine in Qatar and the Arab world

Press Release

Doha, Qatar – Sidra Medicine, a member of Qatar Foundation, has announced that its Chief Research Officer, Prof. Khalid Fakhro, has been named the recipient of the prestigious Arab Award in Genetics by the Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation for Medical and Educational Sciences.

Widely regarded as one of the Arab world’s premier scientific honors, the Arab Award in Genetics is the Foundation’s highest medical award, presented annually to a single scientist whose career-defining breakthroughs have significantly advanced human genetics, genomics, and the clinical management of genetic diseases across the Arab world. 

The recognition celebrates Prof. Fakhro’s contributions to advancing genomic science in the region, including groundbreaking discoveries in the genetics of Arab populations, rare diseases, infertility, and autism spectrum disorder. It also honors his leadership in translating genomic research, bringing scientific innovations closer to the bedside, and enabling more personalized approaches to patient care.

Mr. Mohammad Khalid Al Mana, Acting Chief Executive Officer and Member of the Board of Governors at Sidra Medicine, said: “We are immensely proud of Prof. Khalid Fakhro for receiving this distinguished recognition. His visionary contributions have helped shape the development of genomic research in Qatar and have demonstrated the important role that Arab scientists can play in advancing medical knowledge globally. At Sidra Medicine, his leadership has been instrumental in bringing research and clinical practice closer together, creating new opportunities to improve diagnosis, develop innovative treatments, and deliver more personalized care to patients and families. This award is a testament to his scientific achievements and to the growing impact of Sidra Medicine’s role in the emerging research and innovation from Qatar.”

Prof. Fakhro, who also serves as Chair of the Precision Medicine Program at Sidra Medicine, has played an instrumental role in establishing Qatar as a regional powerhouse for genomic research and precision medicine. Awarded full scholarships throughout his studies, Prof. Fakhro earned his Bachelor’s with honors from the University of Chicago, and his Master’s and PhD from Yale University, where he was selected as a Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) Translational Medicine Scholar. After completing his academic training at Weill Cornell Medical College in New York, he returned to Weill Cornell Medicine Qatar and setup the region’s first human genome sequencing pipelines. 

His foundational research included the first exome-based Mendelian disorders program in Qatar – which has achieved a ~60% diagnostic yield for families with rare disorders – and the development of the first Qatari reference genome map. The latter identified an indigenous Arab founder population with ancestry tracing back to some of the earliest human migrations out of Africa, sparking a paradigm shift in understanding the genetic diversity of GCC populations, and earning the cover of the distinguished scientific journal Genome Research in February 2016. Over the past decade, his laboratory has published more than 100 peer-reviewed studies, mapping genetic variation to health and disease and rectifying the underrepresentation of Arab populations in global genomic databases. Among his signature initiatives are the Qatari Mendelian Program and the BARAKA Study – the region’s largest bioresource dedicated to autism spectrum disorder – alongside landmark discoveries in the genetics of infertility, genome structural variation, the Islamic bioethics of genomic medicine, and the potential benefits of preventive genome sequencing as a screening tool for newborns and children.

Under his executive leadership, Sidra Medicine has strengthened its position as an academic medical center advancing precision medicine through the integration of research, diagnostics, and clinical care. Key milestones include the establishment of Qatar’s first clinical whole-genome sequencing service and its first accredited Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) facility for cell and gene therapies, providing end-to-end service from reading human genomes, to curing rare genetic disease. 

Beyond his research and executive responsibilities, Prof. Fakhro is committed to developing the next generation of scientists and medical researchers. Through his academic appointments at Hamad Bin Khalifa University and Weill Cornell Medicine–Qatar, he has supported the training and mentorship of numerous graduate students and emerging researchers, producing a sustainable talent pipeline in human genome research, and helping strengthen the region’s long-term capabilities in Precision Medicine.

Commenting on the recognition, Prof. Khalid Fakhro said: “I am deeply humbled to receive the Arab Award in Genetics from the Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation. When I began my professional journey two decades ago, my dream was to reverse the regional brain drain and prove that world-class science can be done from within the Arab world, for the Arab world. This recognition really belongs to my dedicated team at Sidra Medicine, our clinical and academic partners across Qatar Foundation, and the thousands of families who have trusted us to advance precision medicine for future generations. Importantly, this is a recognition of the steadfast investment that Qatar has made in biomedical and health sciences over the years, and a testimony to the success of that vision.”

The Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation for Medical and Educational Sciences traces its medical awards program to 1999, when the late Sheikh Hamdan bin Rashid Al Maktoum established an initiative to recognize scientific excellence and contributions to healthcare. The Foundation continues to support medical research, education, and innovation through its awards and scientific initiatives.

About Sidra Medicine

Innovating Care. Transforming Lives

From the heart of Qatar, Sidra Medicine, is a private, not-for-profit academic healthcare and research institution for women, children, and young people.

Established by the Qatar Foundation for Education, Science, and Community Development, Sidra Medicine is committed to delivering exceptional patient and family-focused care, conducting innovative biomedical and clinical research, and providing a personalized journey of care and cure and precision medicine specifically for rare and genetic diseases.
